demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects turnover in silk fabrics to increase in FY26 on rising demand from sports, apparel and home-furnishing textile segments.
- Some customers in the USA and Europe have started shifting textile business away from China toward India, Bangladesh and Vietnam, which management views as an opportunity.
- Trade tensions between China and the USA (import duty increases) are seen as putting the company in a better position to enter low-priced items.
- Global market outlook remains unclear due to the new coronavirus strain, though vaccination progress is expected to help demand …

capex_expansion.body: The bundle discloses no capacity-addition or capex project; the only expansion-adjacent narrative is product-mix broadening (outdoor and contract fabrics) at the existing Nanjangud weaving unit, with no new site, line or capacity figure named.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- High value of fabrics has suppressed demand in European and American markets, forcing a shift to less-expensive product qualities.
- The company must compete against big mills within India even as it repositions its product mix.
- Abnormal increases in input cost combined with lack of clarity on export-benefit rates create uncertainty for manufacturers and exporters.
- The global market outlook remained unclear due to new coronavirus strains, with recovery dependent on vaccination progress worldwide.
- India's share of the global industrial-gloves market is described as very minimal, indicating limited current scale relative to the global opportunity.
- The Sarandi, Ahmedabad yarn/spinning unit suspended manufacturing operations in December 2015 due to steep competition and unfavorable market conditions, and has since operated only as a cotton trading business.
- Management's cautionary statement flags demand-supply conditions, raw material prices, government policy changes, tax regimes, global economic developments, litigation and labor negotiations as factors that could cause actual results to differ materially.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Shifting the silk/velvet product mix to less expensive qualities to strengthen demand in European and American markets.
- Developing new fabrics with anti-microbial and anti-Covid finishes, and expanding the product mix into outdoor and contract fabrics.
- Focusing on sustainable product lines to align with changing brand preferences in fashion markets.
- Positioning to capture textile business shifting from China to India, Bangladesh and Vietnam.
- Taking steps to promote the company's leather and handloom products globally to enhance scale and market share.
